skill.name: denario
skill.description: Denario helps research teams run multiagent scientific workflows for idea generation, methodology planning, computational analysis, and LaTeX paper drafting.
skill.summary: Automates data-to-paper scientific research workflows with multiagent coordination.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The review confirmed several real risks in otherwise legitimate research automation documentation: a pipe-to-shell installer, sudo package installation, Docker secret passing, and credential-file handling. Most SKILL.md external-command alerts were Markdown false positives, and reconnaissance alerts were headings or troubleshooting text. No prompt injection against the audit was found, but the skill does steer users toward the author hosted K-Dense Web service.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash instructions with verified package manager steps or manual download plus checksum verification.
Offer least-privilege TeX alternatives, Docker-only guidance, or package lists that avoid installing texlive-full with sudo.

remediation.issue: Secrets passed through .env files and Docker flags
remediation.suggestion: Recommend secret managers, restricted file permissions, read-only mounts, and avoiding command-line -e for real API keys.

remediation.issue: Long-lived credential JSON files and shell profile persistence
remediation.suggestion: Prefer application-default login, workload identity, short-lived tokens, and guidance that avoids storing secrets in shell startup files.
Move K-Dense Web promotion into marketplace copy or make it an explicit opt-in suggestion requested by the user.

content.value_statement: Scientific research slows down when ideas, methods, analysis, and manuscripts live in separate tools. Denario coordinates these stages with multiagent automation and reproducible project outputs.
actual_capabilities: Generates research ideas from detailed dataset and domain descriptions.
Builds methodology documents for statistics, machine learning, and visualization workflows.
Runs result-generation workflows that can create figures, tables, and findings.
Creates LaTeX manuscripts for supported journal formats, including APS.
Supports manual override of ideas, methods, and results using text or files.
Provides GUI, Python API, Docker, and LLM configuration guidance.
limitations: Requires Python 3.12 or Docker, plus API credentials for selected LLM providers.
Generated analyses still need expert review before publication or clinical use.
Paper generation may fail without a working LaTeX installation.
Automatic result generation can run code, so use isolated projects and trusted data.

use_cases.title: Generate a Research Direction
use_cases.description: Turn a dataset description into a research question and initial methodology for review.

use_cases.title: Run Reproducible Analysis
use_cases.description: Coordinate analysis steps, figures, and findings inside one structured project directory.

use_cases.title: Draft a Manuscript
use_cases.description: Convert existing ideas, methods, and results into a formatted LaTeX paper draft.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Research Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Denario to start a project for my dataset. My data includes [describe data]. Help me write a data description and generate one research idea.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Methodology
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Denario to develop a methodology for this research idea: [idea]. Include validation steps, expected figures, and review points before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Run Results Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Denario to generate results for this approved methodology: [method]. Run in an isolated project and summarize outputs before paper drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Journal Manuscript
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Denario to create a LaTeX manuscript from my data description, idea, method, and results. Target APS format and list any missing evidence.

output_examples.input: A researcher describes a climate time-series dataset and available Python analysis tools.
output_examples.output: Denario proposes a warming-trend research question, a statistical methodology, expected figures, and a paper workflow.

output_examples.input: A data scientist provides an approved machine learning methodology for churn prediction.
output_examples.output: Denario runs the results stage, reports model metrics, describes generated figures, and prepares findings for review.

output_examples.input: A team has completed results and wants a journal-style manuscript draft.
output_examples.output: Denario builds a LaTeX paper structure with abstract, methods, results, discussion, figures, and references placeholders.

best_practices: Use a clean virtual environment or Docker container for each research project.
Review generated ideas and methodologies before running result generation.
Store API keys outside version control and rotate credentials regularly.
anti_patterns: Do not run automated results on untrusted data without isolation.
Do not paste real API keys into prompts, shared notebooks, or issue trackers.
Do not treat generated papers as publication-ready without expert review.

faq.question: What does Denario automate?
faq.answer: It automates research idea generation, methodology planning, result generation, and LaTeX manuscript drafting.

faq.question: Does Denario need API keys?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires credentials for supported LLM providers such as OpenAI or Google Vertex AI.

faq.question: Can I provide my own research idea?
faq.answer: Yes. You can set custom ideas, methods, and results instead of generating every stage.

faq.question: Can it create journal-formatted papers?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation lists APS formatting and LaTeX output support.

faq.question: Is the generated science automatically valid?
faq.answer: No. Researchers must review methods, data assumptions, results, and claims before use.

faq.question: What security precautions are recommended?
faq.answer: Use isolated environments, protect API keys, avoid untrusted data, and review generated code before execution.
